new_statements.quote: Word stress is relatively light, falling regularly on the ultima, with secondary stress in longer words. The ultimate stress is not restricted to the root, but on nouns it falls on the final syllable of personal possessive suffixes, and on verbs it shifts to the final syllable of personal object suffixes. Other suffixes, such as clause markers on verbs and locative and instrumental suffixes on nouns, are never stressed.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word core = root plus any personal (possessive or object) pronominal suffix; outer suffixes (tense-mood-aspect / clause markers on verbs, locative and instrumental suffixes on nouns) are unstressable and fall outside the stress domain, so a word ending in such a suffix has stress on the syllable immediately preceding it. Stress is phonetically weak ('relatively light').
new_statements.secondary_stress: 'with secondary stress in longer words' -- position not specified.
new_statements.exceptions: Clause-marker (T-M-A) suffixes on verbs and locative/instrumental suffixes on nouns are never stressed (stress stays on the final syllable of root+pronominal suffix). No lexical exceptions mentioned.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement for the mission standard (Gedaged Island dialect, p.855); domain is root + personal pronominal suffixes, excluding outer TMA/locative/instrumental suffixes. Impressionistic description by a long-term Lutheran missionary user of the language, in a 10-page lingua-franca chapter, not a full grammar. Mager 1952 marks accent per dictionary entry (per HTRC token evidence), which could indicate less than full predictability -- to be checked against Mager's Explanatory Notes.
new_statements.identity_note: Freyberg describes the Lutheran mission standard 'Bel (Gedaged)', explicitly based on the dialect of Gedaged Island in Madang Harbour (p.855), with Siar and Bilia dialects said to differ only slightly; this is Gedaged proper, glottocode geda1237 / ISO gdd (older names Graged, Ragetta, Mitebog, Szeak-Bagili). Not to be confused with Z'graggen's 'Belan' family label covering Bilbil, Takia, Megiar, Matukar.

sources.note: p.856 sect. 7.4.5.4.2.2: word stress light, regularly on the ultima, secondary stress in longer words; on nouns stress falls on the final syllable of personal possessive suffixes, on verbs on the final syllable of personal object suffixes; clause-marker (TMA) suffixes on verbs and locative/instrumental suffixes on nouns are never stressed.
